sections.content:
112,440 people

were counted on the census as "information technology directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Information technology directors organise and co-ordinate the work and resources necessary to provide and operate IT infrastructure and services, including networks, devices, servers and software that runs on the infrastructure within an organisation.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "information technology directors" there were more men than women (82.8% compared with 17.2%).

This means "information technology directors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 82.8% and women made up 17.2% of "information technology directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "information technology directors" included:

  • directors in logistics, warehousing and transport
  • cyber security professionals
  • waste disposal and environmental services managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "information technology directors", 19.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "information technology directors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "information technology directors" included:

  • head teachers and principals
  • public relations and communications directors
  • functional managers and directors (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "information technology directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "information technology directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "information technology directors", 6.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.3% compared with 13.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (67.6%) than self-employed (32.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
